Definition: Stock symbol, for example 'KO'.
Sector name, used to compare a stock with its peers.
Date of the data snapshot a row describes.
Forward annual dividend per share, in dollars.
Forward dividend yield: dividend_rate divided by share price. Yahoo's dividendYield appeared as a percent in the MSFT sample (0.95 meant 0.95%), so divide by 100 to store a fraction.
Dividends paid over the last 12 months divided by price. Already a fraction in the MSFT sample.
Average yield over five years, used as a baseline for the current yield. A percent in the MSFT sample, so divide by 100.
dividend_yield divided by five_year_avg_dividend_yield. A value well above 1 can mean the price fell on bad news, not that the income improved.
Share of earnings paid out as dividends. Above 1.0 means the company pays out more than it earns. A fraction in the MSFT sample.
Most recent ex-dividend date. yfinance may return a Unix timestamp that has to be converted to a date.
Number of shares outstanding, used to turn the per-share dividend into a total dividend bill.
free_cashflow divided by total dividends (dividend_rate times shares_outstanding). Below 1 means free cash flow does not cover the dividend.
Consecutive years the annual dividend increased, counted from the dividend history. Stretch goal.
Sensitivity to market moves. Above 1 means the stock swings more than the market.
Annualized standard deviation of daily returns over the last 252 trading days (daily standard deviation times the square root of 252). Needs a price-history backfill.
Largest peak-to-trough fall in closing price over the last year, as a negative fraction.
Total debt relative to shareholder equity (leverage). Yahoo's value appeared percent-style in the MSFT sample (31.5 meant 0.315), so divide by 100 for a plain ratio. Often missing for banks.
Current assets divided by current liabilities: the ability to cover short-term bills.
Operating cash flow minus capital spending, in dollars.
Overall governance risk score published by Yahoo. Confirm which direction is riskier before using it.
Price divided by earnings per share over the trailing 12 months (TTM). Negative or missing means no profits.
Price divided by expected earnings for the next 12 months.
1 if dividend_rate is greater than 0, else 0. Limits the universe to dividend payers.
1 if payout_ratio is between 0 and 1 (earnings cover the dividend), else 0. The threshold is the team's decision.
1 if free_cashflow is greater than 0, else 0.
1 if fcf_dividend_coverage is at least 1, else 0.
1 if every field needed for the score is present and plausible, else 0. Missing values are excluded, never filled with 0.
Sum of the flag fields. The pass cutoff is the team's decision (the Deep Value example kept stocks scoring 5 or more out of 9).
Z-score of winsorized volatility_1y (1st and 99th percentile), inverted so a higher z means lower risk.
Z-score of winsorized beta, inverted so a higher z means lower risk.
Z-score of winsorized debt_to_equity, inverted so a higher z means lower leverage.
Z-score of winsorized dividend_yield, not inverted.
Z-score of winsorized fcf_dividend_coverage, not inverted.
Weighted sum of the safety z-scores (z_volatility, z_beta, z_debt_to_equity). Weights are the team's decision (TBD).
Weighted sum of the income z-scores (z_dividend_yield, z_fcf_coverage). Weights are the team's decision (TBD).
Low, Medium, or High, from cutoffs on safety_composite (for example the top third is Low). The cutoffs are the team's decision (TBD).
Low, Medium, or High, chosen by the user and matched against risk_level.
Google GenAI SDK client (genai.Client()) used to call Gemini. The API key is read from an environment variable and never stored in code or the repo.
Gemini model identifier. The class example uses 'gemini-2.5-flash'; confirm the model with the professor.
Gemini's explanation of the top-ranked stocks. It may use only the numbers passed in from the database and must not supply figures of its own.
